A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymptotic expansion of Feynman integrals in terms of powers in the momentum squared is a useful method for the evaluation of Feynman graphs.
the small momentum expansion of the Feynman diagrams can be used as an alternative to the asymptotic expansion for large masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotic expansion of a diagram in large masses can be continued to zero mass.
the asymptotic expansion of the Feynman integrals in terms of the large masses can be used to obtain the small momentum expansion of the integrals.
it is sufficient to consider the small momentum expansion of the diagrams, which are needed in the limit of zero threshold, to obtain the correct result for all values of the momentum.
